title: How Tutankhamun's Tomb Was Found After 3,000 Years
hook: Nearly every royal tomb in the Valley was robbed. Only one came down to us almost complete, and it belonged to a king almost nobody remembered.
thumbnail_picture: Huge close-up on the right of a golden pharaoh's death mask glowing in the dark, lit by a single candle; on the left edge a tired 1920s Englishman in a pith helmet and dusty waistcoat gasps, eyes wide, face lit gold. Deep black stone tomb background.
description:
How was Tutankhamun's tomb found after 3,000 years? Follow Howard Carter, nearly out of money, on his last dig season in the Valley of the Kings in 1922.

Why did a small tomb survive when the grand tombs of mightier pharaohs were emptied, and how did a forgotten boy king become the best-known pharaoh of all? This is the true story of the sealed door, the candle, and "wonderful things".

Sources: Howard Carter and A. C. Mace, "The Tomb of Tut-ankh-Amen" (1923-33); Nicholas Reeves, "The Complete Tutankhamun"; the Griffith Institute, University of Oxford, Tutankhamun archive; the Egyptian Museum, Cairo; Zahi Hawass et al., "Ancestry and Pathology in King Tutankhamun's Family", JAMA (2010).

Animation and narration are AI-assisted; script reviewed by a human.

scenes.narration: Nearly every royal tomb in the Valley was robbed. Only one came down to us almost complete, and it belonged to a king almost nobody remembered.
scenes.caption: THE ONE LEFT
scenes.picture: A solid gold coffin shaped like a young pharaoh gleaming in a dark small stone chamber, lit by a single flickering candle, dust floating in the air

scenes.narration: Why did this tiny tomb survive when the grand ones were emptied? The answer starts with a man running out of money.
scenes.caption: THE QUESTION
scenes.picture: A tired Englishman in a dusty waistcoat and pith helmet standing alone at the edge of a sunbaked rocky valley, empty pockets turned out, worried face

scenes.narration: His name was Howard Carter, and in 1922 his patron was ready to end the funding. Carter would get one last season.
scenes.caption: HOWARD CARTER
scenes.picture: Close-up portrait of Howard Carter, a mustached Englishman in his late forties in a felt hat, squinting in harsh Egyptian sunlight, determined face

scenes.narration: His battlefield was the Valley of the Kings, a glaring canyon of limestone cliffs near Luxor.
scenes.caption: VALLEY OF THE KINGS
scenes.picture: Wide view of a dry glaring limestone canyon with pale cliffs and rubble slopes under a white-hot sky, tiny diggers far below, no buildings

scenes.narration: For five centuries, pharaohs were buried here in tombs cut deep into the rock. But the thieves arrived.
scenes.caption: THE ROBBERS
scenes.picture: Ancient Egyptian thieves in plain linen kilts creeping at night with oil lamps toward a cliff-cut tomb entrance in a desert canyon, shadows stretching

scenes.narration: So almost every tomb was looted. Gold gone, mummies stripped, painted rooms left bare.
scenes.caption: EMPTIED
scenes.picture: An ancient Egyptian burial chamber with painted walls, a broken empty stone sarcophagus, scattered shards of pottery and nothing of gold left, dusty light

scenes.narration: Carter knew this valley's story. He'd come to Egypt at seventeen to copy tomb paintings, with no degree, just sharp eyes and stubbornness.
scenes.caption: AN OUTSIDER
scenes.picture: A teenage English boy in 1890s clothes kneeling in an Egyptian tomb, carefully painting a copy of a colorful wall painting by lamplight

scenes.narration: That stubbornness made him believe a young king named Tutankhamun was still waiting somewhere in the valley. Almost nobody agreed.
scenes.caption: A HUNCH
scenes.picture: Howard Carter in a tent at night leaning over a table covered with rough sketches of rocky ground, an oil lamp lighting his thoughtful face

scenes.narration: One rich American, Theodore Davis, had dug here for years. In 1912 he declared the valley exhausted.
scenes.caption: "EXHAUSTED"
scenes.picture: A stout, confident American gentleman in a white suit and straw hat waving a hand dismissively before a long rocky valley of spoil heaps, 1912

scenes.narration: Davis had found only a few scraps with the boy king's name, so he thought that was all there was.
scenes.caption: JUST SCRAPS
scenes.picture: Close-up of a worker's hands holding a small blue-green faience cup and a crumpled piece of gold foil over a wooden crate

scenes.narration: Carter needed money to prove him wrong. His partner was Lord Carnarvon, a wealthy English aristocrat who paid for every dig.
scenes.caption: LORD CARNARVON
scenes.picture: An elegant English lord in a tweed suit and cap, mustache, seated on a folding chair outside a dig tent, arms crossed, desert behind him

scenes.narration: The First World War stopped everything. Afterward, they searched square by square, trench by trench.
scenes.caption: THE SEARCH
scenes.picture: Dozens of Egyptian workers in white galabiyas digging long trenches in the valley floor, baskets of rubble passed hand to hand, dust clouds in the sun

scenes.narration: But five seasons passed. Mountains of rubble were moved, and they found almost nothing.
scenes.caption: NOTHING
scenes.picture: Huge pale heaps of dug-out rubble towering over a quiet valley, one lone worker sitting on a stone, shoulders slumped, late afternoon

scenes.narration: So by 1922, Carnarvon was ready to pull the plug. The money was draining away, and the valley looked empty.
scenes.caption: FUNDING ENDS
scenes.picture: Lord Carnarvon in a shaded tent shaking his head, hand raised to stop, while Carter stands facing him, jaw tight, 1920s desert camp

scenes.narration: Carter refused to quit. By his own account, he offered to pay for one more season himself.
scenes.caption: ALL IN
scenes.picture: Howard Carter standing firm, pointing with one finger at the ground outside a tent, determined face, golden sunset light

scenes.narration: That convinced Carnarvon to keep paying. One last season, on a patch of ground Carter had skipped for years.
scenes.caption: ONE MORE SEASON
scenes.picture: Two Englishmen in 1920s clothes shaking hands over a camp table, warm lamp light, tent interior, serious faces

scenes.narration: It lay under old workmen's huts, right beside the tomb of Ramesses the Sixth. Tourists walked over it every day.
scenes.caption: UNDER THE HUTS
scenes.picture: Crumbled ancient stone workmen's huts on a rocky slope beside the entrance of a large royal tomb, tourists in 1920s hats walking past

scenes.narration: So on November 4th, 1922, workers began clearing the ground beneath those huts.
scenes.caption: NOVEMBER 4, 1922
scenes.picture: Egyptian workers in white galabiyas shoveling away piles of chipped limestone from beneath ruined huts, early morning light, dust rising

scenes.narration: Then, according to legend, a water boy found a stone step cut into the rock.
scenes.caption: THE FIRST STEP
scenes.picture: A young Egyptian water boy with a clay jar on his shoulder pointing down at a single rough stone step emerging from sand

scenes.narration: Hands brushed away sand. Another step appeared. Then another, leading down into the dark.
scenes.caption: GOING DOWN
scenes.picture: Close-up of dusty hands brushing sand from a descending rock-cut stairway, steps vanishing into shadow

scenes.narration: By the next day, twelve steps were clear. And at the bottom stood a door.
scenes.caption: A SEALED DOOR
scenes.picture: A long rock-cut staircase descending to a plastered stone doorway at the bottom, workers peering down from above, shafts of sunlight

scenes.narration: The plaster was stamped with the necropolis seal, the mark of a guarded graveyard. At first glance, the door looked untouched.
scenes.caption: UNTOUCHED?
scenes.picture: Close-up of an ancient plastered stone door covered in rows of small round clay seal stamps, Carter's hand reaching out but not touching

scenes.narration: Carter's heart must have been pounding. So what did he do? He covered it back up.
scenes.caption: HE WAITED
scenes.picture: Egyptian workers refilling a stairway with rubble under Carter's watch, guards with rifles posted nearby, dusk

scenes.narration: Then he telegraphed Carnarvon in England: a magnificent tomb, seals intact. Come at once.
scenes.caption: THE TELEGRAM
scenes.picture: Howard Carter at a small Luxor telegraph office counter handing a paper to a clerk in a fez, brass equipment, excited expression

scenes.narration: Nearly three weeks later, Carnarvon arrived. They cleared the stairs again, and Carter looked closer at that door.
scenes.caption: A CLOSER LOOK
scenes.picture: Carter crouching with a magnifying glass inspecting the plastered door at the bottom of the cleared stairway, Carnarvon behind him in a cap

scenes.narration: Something was wrong. Only now did he see it: parts of the door had been broken open, then plastered shut again.
scenes.caption: CLUE
scenes.picture: Close-up of a patched section on an ancient stone door where fresh-looking plaster covers a hole, different from the older plaster around it

scenes.narration: Someone had been inside. Thieves, in ancient times. Could anything possibly be left?
scenes.caption: ROBBED?
scenes.picture: Carter and Carnarvon standing in the narrow stairwell, faces falling, shadows on the walls, worried expressions

scenes.narration: Behind the first door was a passage packed with rubble. At its end, a second sealed door.
scenes.caption: A SECOND DOOR
scenes.picture: A narrow rock-cut corridor filled with white chunks of rubble, workers passing baskets out, a second plastered door visible at the far end in lamplight

scenes.narration: November 26th. Carter chiseled a tiny hole and felt hot air rush out. He pushed a candle through.
scenes.caption: THE HOLE
scenes.picture: Close-up of Carter's hands holding a candle and a small iron rod at a tiny chiseled hole in a plastered door, flame leaning in the escaping air

scenes.narration: Behind him, Carnarvon couldn't bear the silence. "Can you see anything?"
scenes.caption: "CAN YOU SEE?"
scenes.picture: Lord Carnarvon in the dim passage leaning anxiously over Carter's shoulder, lit by candlelight, eyes wide, mouth open

scenes.narration: Carter answered: "Yes. Wonderful things."
scenes.caption: WONDERFUL THINGS
scenes.picture: Extreme close-up of Carter's eye at a small hole, golden glints reflected in it, candlelight flickering on his cheek

scenes.narration: Gold everywhere. Couches carved like beasts, painted chests, statues, chariots piled on top of each other.
scenes.caption: GOLD EVERYWHERE
scenes.picture: A cramped chamber crammed with gilded animal-headed couches, painted wooden chests, black and gold statues and chariot parts, lit by flickering candle

scenes.narration: But look at the mess. Boxes were forced open, things shoved aside, as if someone tidied in a hurry.
scenes.caption: A MESS
scenes.picture: Close-up of a jumbled heap of opened painted boxes, spilled jewelry and tossed linen on the floor of a stone chamber, dust and gold glints

scenes.narration: Historians think robbers broke in twice, soon after the burial. But why did they leave so much?
scenes.caption: THE PUZZLE
scenes.picture: Two ancient Egyptian thieves in loincloths crouched in a dark tomb corridor, one holding a small oil jar and glancing nervously back toward the entrance

scenes.narration: One theory is that they were caught, and the officials resealed the tomb. The thieves got away with only oils and small gold.
scenes.caption: THEORY: CAUGHT
scenes.picture: Ancient Egyptian necropolis guards with spears and bronze-bladed khopesh shouting in a tomb entrance, thief running away clutching a small jar

scenes.narration: If that's right, the officials patched the door, stamped it again, and carried on. The tomb was still known, still guarded.
scenes.caption: RESEALED
scenes.picture: An Egyptian official in a white kilt supervising a mason who is applying fresh plaster to a stone doorway, clay seal in his hand, oil lamp

scenes.narration: So what hid it for good? The answer was above. Nearly two centuries later, workers cut the tomb of Ramesses the Sixth.
scenes.caption: THE CLUE ABOVE
scenes.picture: Ancient Egyptian workers hacking a new tomb entrance into a cliff just above a hidden older stairway, limestone chips flying

scenes.narration: Chips of limestone rained down and buried the old entrance. Flash floods packed the rubble tight.
scenes.caption: BURIED
scenes.picture: A flash flood of muddy water carrying white limestone rubble down a rocky valley slope, burying a stairway entrance, stormy sky

scenes.narration: Then the workmen built their huts right on top, never knowing a king lay beneath their feet.
scenes.caption: HUTS ON TOP
scenes.picture: Ancient Egyptian laborers in kilts building crude stone huts on a heap of rubble, cooking pots and smoke, a hidden slope beneath

scenes.narration: The entrance vanished. With time, the memory of where it lay was probably lost. And the king himself was fading from memory.
scenes.caption: LOST
scenes.picture: A quiet empty desert valley at dusk with smooth rubble slopes hiding everything, a lone hawk circling, no people

scenes.narration: Why forgotten? Tutankhamun became pharaoh at about nine years old. He would die roughly ten years later.
scenes.caption: A BOY KING
scenes.picture: A small ancient Egyptian boy of nine in a heavy gold collar and blue crown sitting stiffly on a large throne, adult advisers standing around

scenes.narration: Historians think his father, Akhenaten, pushed the sun-disc Aten above the old gods, and shocked the whole country.
scenes.caption: A SHOCKED EGYPT
scenes.picture: A tall ancient Egyptian pharaoh with an elongated face raising his arms to a bright sun disc with rays, priests of old gods looking angry in the background

scenes.narration: Then the boy's advisers restored the old gods. The temples came back to life.
scenes.caption: UNDOING IT
scenes.picture: Ancient Egyptian priests in white linen carrying a golden statue of a god in procession into a restored temple with tall columns, crowd cheering

scenes.narration: But after he died, later kings scrubbed that whole family from the records. Tutankhamun's name vanished with them.
scenes.caption: ERASED
scenes.picture: An ancient Egyptian stonemason with a chisel chipping smooth a blank carved wall, stone dust falling, torchlight

scenes.narration: And his tomb was small. Historians think his death was unexpected, and the tomb was a small, possibly borrowed one, finished in a hurry.
scenes.caption: A RUSH JOB
scenes.picture: Ancient Egyptian workers hurriedly plastering and painting a small rough tomb chamber by torchlight, ladders and paint pots, urgent mood

scenes.narration: So the shield was never magic. It was luck, rubble, and being forgotten. <short pause> Then the best part began.
scenes.caption: LUCK, NOT MAGIC
scenes.picture: A cliff face in the Valley of the Kings at golden hour with rubble slopes and a hidden stairway entrance barely visible, still and quiet

scenes.narration: In February 1923, Carter opened the burial chamber. Four gold shrines stood nested inside each other like boxes.
scenes.caption: THE BURIAL ROOM
scenes.picture: A burial chamber almost filled by a huge gilded wooden shrine glowing in lamplight, Carter small at its side, gold walls shining

scenes.narration: A year later, the stone sarcophagus lid was lifted, and three coffins lay inside. The innermost was solid gold, over a hundred kilos of it.
scenes.caption: SOLID GOLD
scenes.picture: Carter and two assistants lifting the lid of a stone sarcophagus, revealing a gleaming gold coffin in the shape of a pharaoh, lamplight

scenes.narration: On the king's face lay a mask of gold inlaid with lapis and glass, weighing about ten kilos.
scenes.caption: THE MASK
scenes.picture: Close-up of the golden death mask of a young pharaoh with blue stripes and deep dark eyes, lit by lamp, dust floating

scenes.narration: Beneath it rested a young man of about eighteen. The boy nobody remembered. And then, trouble.
scenes.caption: THE BOY
scenes.picture: A reverent view of an ancient wrapped mummy of a young man with a small gold ornament, resting in a dim chamber, soft light

scenes.narration: In April 1923, Lord Carnarvon died in Cairo of blood poisoning, after an infected mosquito bite.
scenes.caption: CARNARVON DIES
scenes.picture: Lord Carnarvon pale and weak lying in a bed in a 1920s Cairo hotel room, a doctor in a white coat at his side, dim lamp

scenes.narration: Newspapers screamed about a pharaoh's curse. But that was a myth. Carter lived on until 1939, and so did most of his team.
scenes.caption: THE CURSE?
scenes.picture: A 1920s newsboy in a flat cap shouting and waving a newspaper on a busy London street, wide-eyed passers-by in coats

scenes.narration: The real work was slow. Carter's team catalogued over five thousand objects, and it took them about ten years.
scenes.caption: 5,000+ OBJECTS
scenes.picture: Carter and an assistant kneeling in a makeshift tomb-lab cataloguing hundreds of golden objects laid on tables in lamplight

scenes.narration: So why is he the best-known pharaoh? Because we found his burial nearly complete.
scenes.caption: THE ANSWER
scenes.picture: A glowing gold throne with a carved scene of a young king and queen, sitting in a dark room with a single beam of light on it

scenes.narration: Ramesses the Second built temples across the land. But his tomb was stripped. Tut's was a time capsule.
scenes.caption: TIME CAPSULE
scenes.picture: A vast ancient Egyptian temple facade with giant seated colossi statues in bright sun, contrasted by an empty ransacked tomb doorway in the foreground

scenes.narration: A dagger of iron from a meteorite. A golden throne. Even sandals.
scenes.caption: EVERYDAY LIFE
scenes.picture: A display of a gleaming dagger with a gold handle, a pair of delicate gold-trimmed sandals, and a gilded throne on a dark table

scenes.narration: And a world tired of war fell in love. Crowds, fashion, films, even jewelry copied the pharaoh.
scenes.caption: TUT-MANIA
scenes.picture: A 1920s fashion shop window with a mannequin wearing a gold Egyptian-style headband and beaded dress, crowds of well-dressed people admiring it

scenes.narration: In 1972, the treasures went to London. About one point seven million people queued to see them.
scenes.caption: 1.7 MILLION
scenes.picture: A very long queue of 1970s Londoners in coats winding around a grand museum building, umbrellas, patient faces, overcast sky

scenes.narration: Studies suggest he was frail, probably used a cane, and had malaria. His cause of death is still debated. Not mighty. Just human.
scenes.caption: JUST A BOY
scenes.picture: A thin young Egyptian king in a simple linen kilt leaning on a carved wooden walking stick in a sunlit palace courtyard, thoughtful face

scenes.narration: So the best-known king of all got there by being forgotten, his tomb buried under rubble.
scenes.caption: THE POINT
scenes.picture: Wide golden-hour view of the Valley of the Kings with the small hidden tomb entrance in the rocks, a tiny figure standing before it

scenes.narration: Carter bet his last season on a patch of ground everyone had walked past. Being forgotten was the best guard the boy ever had.
scenes.caption: THE LAST BET
scenes.picture: Howard Carter alone at the bottom of the stairway at dusk holding a lantern before the opened doorway, golden light spilling onto his face

narrator: Gripping investigative storyteller, low and intense, leaning in, building suspense, quick between clues.
